title: Focus Deck Copy Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · 15 October 2026 · Unblock · parent issue #21 (Focus Deck copy)
replyPrefix: Build plan approved: Focus Deck copy

short.lead: This is how the approved design gets built: a GitHub issues switch that starts off, then a button that copies Focus Deck's data into Unblock with the issue links cut, then a check in a real browser. Each step has its own GitHub issue, under one parent issue for the whole feature.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it does and what it needs from you.
items: #22: a GitHub issues switch, off to start with

One check inside ghFetch (app/js/github.js:11), the function that every GitHub request goes through. While the switch is off, it refuses every issue, label and repo request, and lets Unblock's own Gist sync through. Auto-sync does not start and shows no error, and Settings gets a checkbox for turning the switch on.
#23: the Copy from Focus Deck button

It finds the Gist that holds focus-deck-state.json, reads it without writing to it, cuts the issue links in the copy, and merges the result into Unblock's own Gist. Settings then says how many projects and tasks were copied and how many links were cut.
#24: a real-browser check and the write-up

A script runs the app in Chromium (a browser) against a fake Focus Deck Gist and records every request. The check fails if anything other than a read touches that Gist, or if any issue request goes out while the switch is off.
Once the three steps pass, open Unblock with your own data and press Copy from Focus Deck.
Copy your data, then confirm Focus Deck still shows everything unchanged.

changes: Off to start with, so Unblock stays away from the GitHub issues that Focus Deck also uses.
The setting is stored on each device under the name unblock-github-issues, so a new device also starts with it off.
Today, Unblock imports issues from up to 20 of your repos whenever you save a GitHub token.
No issue is read or written until you turn the switch on.
Unblock and Focus Deck can't change each other's GitHub issues.
Copies your projects and tasks once, with the issue links cut.
Each unlinked task is also added to Unblock's list of excluded issues, so if you turn the switch on later, Unblock does not import the same issue a second time next to the copied task.
Today, Unblock starts with no projects or tasks.
After the copy, Unblock has all of Focus Deck's projects and tasks.
Focus Deck's Gist is only ever read.
choices: Where should an unlinked task keep its issue reference?
At the end of the title
The title becomes, for example, "Fix login (Ajw2003/focus-deck-app#12)". You can see the reference straight away, and no new screen code is needed.
The title stays clean, but the reference is invisible until a later change shows it somewhere.

I recommend the end of the title. Tasks have no notes field, so the title is the only place where you would see the reference without new screen code. A hidden field would keep it out of sight until a later change adds a place to show it.
